transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I understand Press 6 is available tonight for the customer validation campaign on the polymer housings — 1,200 pieces on the overnight shift. Before I can approve this campaign and finalize the operating plan, I need to make sure we've got our pre-shift check-in lined up with maintenance and EHS per company procedure. I also want to confirm the standard 50-piece trial is still part of the plan before we release to full production. Who's here from maintenance and EHS so we can start coordinating?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something before we go further. My inspection of Press 6 found the platen alignment is 0.7 millimeters out of tolerance. The alignment service has to be completed before the press can run, and it takes exactly 4 hours. I recorded the measurement in my maintenance notebook, but I have to be transparent — the work order hasn't been entered into the maintenance system yet. We'll need to account for that 4-hour service window tonight before any trial or production run can start.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Good morning, Marisol. I need to flag a serious EHS concern before we proceed. My preliminary air reading near Press 6 came back at 85 parts per million of the solvent in the new release agent — that's well above our EHS limit of 50 parts per million. Until we get readings at or below 50 ppm, this campaign will require local exhaust ventilation and continuous VOC monitoring in place. I'm still waiting on lab confirmation before I can update the area permit, but we need to plan around these controls tonight.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text:
Thank you both for flagging these issues — this is exactly why we do the pre-shift check-in. Let me work through what I'm hearing:

Theo, so Press 6 needs a 4-hour platen alignment service before anything can run — that's a hard prerequisite. And the work order still needs to be entered into the maintenance system. Can you get that entered now so we have it documented?

Priya, the 85 ppm reading is well above the 50 ppm EHS limit. So tonight's campaign will absolutely require local exhaust ventilation and continuous VOC monitoring, and we can't proceed until readings are at or below 50 ppm. I understand you're waiting on lab confirmation before updating the area permit — do we have the LEV and VOC monitoring equipment available and ready to deploy tonight?

Here's what I'm thinking for the operating plan so far:
1. Theo enters the work order and completes the 4-hour alignment service first.
2. Priya gets LEV and continuous VOC monitoring set up, and we need confirmed readings at or below 50 ppm before any run starts.
3. Once both of those are cleared, we run the standard 50-piece trial.
4. If the trial passes inspection, we release to the full 1,200-piece production run.

The 4-hour service window plus setup time for EHS controls is going to eat into the overnight shift. I need both of you to confirm timelines so I can decide whether we can realistically complete the trial and the full 1,200 pieces tonight, or whether we need to adjust the plan. What are your time estimates?
transcript.speaker: A1
